themes_detail.label: Traffic Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic-related 311 complaints spiked to 6 complaints last week versus a 1.2-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 380% increase (z-score: 5.73)—suggesting a sudden deterioration in traffic conditions or enforcement in Crown Heights/Prospect Heights that warrants investigation into causes and scope.
evidence: 6 traffic complaints last week vs. 1.2 weekly average over 8-week baseline (380% increase)
Z-score of 5.73 indicates statistically significant spike
Pattern emerged within last 2 weeks, making it newly acute
reporting_angles: Interview DOT about recent road work, lane closures, or signal changes on major Crown Heights corridors
Canvass residents on Nostrand Ave, Brooklyn Ave, or Atlantic Ave for specific complaints about congestion or dangerous conditions

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Violations Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining 311 complaints rocketed to 3 complaints 3 weeks ago from a 0.2-per-week baseline—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35, highest severity)—indicating either rapid expansion of outdoor dining infrastructure or systematic violations of regulations in the district.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase)
Highest z-score among all spikes (6.35), indicating most statistically significant anomaly
Suggests concentrated activity in a small window, likely tied to seasonal expansion or specific streets
reporting_angles: Map outdoor dining permits and violations on Franklin Ave, Nostrand Ave, or Bedford Ave to identify hotspot blocks
Interview community board and SLA about outdoor dining expansion post-pandemic and enforcement gaps
Document whether complaints are about safety, sanitation, or illegal sheds taking up sidewalk space

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage & Construction Chaos
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 6 complaints 2 weeks ago versus 1.0 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 4.47), paired with general construction/plumbing complaints jumping to 38 complaints 3 weeks ago versus 13.2 average (187% spike)—suggesting uncoordinated or unmonitored construction activity harming the streetscape.
evidence: 6 illegal tree damage complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (500% increase, z-score: 4.47)
38 construction/plumbing complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 13.2 weekly average (187% increase, z-score: 4.06)
474 total DOB permit filings in last 90 days (288 alterations, 97 new buildings), suggesting heavy construction activity
Converges with Community Board's repeated budget request for 'Assign additional building inspectors'
reporting_angles: Request DOB inspection records to identify which construction sites are generating tree damage complaints and violations
Interview Parks Department about tree preservation enforcement during active construction periods
Cross-reference permit data with complaint locations to identify repeat offender contractors or blocks

themes_detail.label: Electrical & Hazmat Safety Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints jumped to 3 complaints 2 weeks ago from a 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42), and hazardous materials complaints spiked to 5 complaints 3 weeks ago versus 0.9 baseline (471% increase, z-score: 3.92)—signaling potential infrastructure failures or unsafe building conditions that could endanger residents.
evidence: 3 electrical complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
5 hazardous materials complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (471% increase, z-score: 3.92)
3 asbestos complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 average (300% increase, z-score: 3.4)
Suggests clustering of environmental/safety hazards, possibly related to renovation or demolition activity
reporting_angles: Obtain FDNY incident reports for electrical fires or electrical system failures in the district over past 3 weeks
Interview NYC Department of Environmental Protection about hazmat complaints and whether they cluster around specific buildings or construction sites
Request Department of Health asbestos abatement records to determine if complaints reflect inadequate disclosure or improper removal

themes_detail.label: Obstruction & Street Access Blockages
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints spiked to 6 complaints 3 weeks ago versus 2.1 weekly average (182% increase, z-score: 3.68), likely driven by outdoor dining sheds, construction debris, or street furniture encroaching on pedestrian space—compounding accessibility and safety concerns.
evidence: 6 obstruction complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly average (182% increase, z-score: 3.68)
Converges with outdoor dining spike (3 weeks ago) and construction activity (474 recent permits), suggesting multiple sources of blockages
Likely compounds sidewalk accessibility issues for seniors and disabled residents, which aligns with CB budget request for 'outreach services to homebound older adults'
reporting_angles: Walk Crown Heights commercial corridors to document outdoor dining sheds, construction barriers, and other obstructions blocking sidewalks
Interview advocates for disabled residents about accessibility complaints during and after construction
Request 311 complaint detail to determine whether obstructions are outdoor dining sheds, construction equipment, or other sources
